title: AI Security Research Graph - Research Seed
research_disclosure: Primary-source pages and abstracts were checked; no experiments were reproduced, and listed videos were not watched. Source-linked does not mean all primary papers were reviewed in full.

nodes.title: Refusal-direction ablation / abliteration
nodes.summary: Refusal-related interventions may use activation ablation or derived weight edits; narrower than removing every safeguard.

nodes.title: ControlNet-style conditioning
nodes.summary: Add structured conditioning pathways to a generative pipeline.

nodes.title: Knowledge distillation
nodes.summary: Teacher-student transfer can be authorized development or support unauthorized functional imitation.

nodes.title: DreamBooth personalization
nodes.summary: Subject-specific diffusion fine-tuning; neutral personalization technique.

nodes.title: Full-parameter fine-tuning
nodes.summary: Update most or all model weights for a new objective; neutral adaptation.

nodes.title: LoRA
nodes.summary: Train low-rank update matrices; malicious behavior depends on data, objective and deployment.

nodes.title: Targeted model editing
nodes.summary: Modify selected learned associations; locality and side effects require evaluation.

nodes.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
nodes.summary: Adapt a subset or added parameters rather than all model weights.

nodes.title: Prefix tuning
nodes.summary: Learn continuous prefixes while freezing base parameters.

nodes.title: QLoRA
nodes.summary: Combine quantized base weights with low-rank adaptation; neither a model format nor an attack.

nodes.title: Representation engineering
nodes.summary: Analyze or modify internal representations; neutral methodological umbrella.

nodes.title: Soft prompt tuning
nodes.summary: Learn prompt embeddings rather than authoring ordinary discrete text prompts.

nodes.title: Activation steering
nodes.summary: Change runtime representations using a chosen intervention and appropriate activation access.

nodes.title: Textual inversion
nodes.summary: Learned concept embeddings for generation; not the same concept as privacy model inversion.

nodes.title: Machine unlearning and concept erasure
nodes.summary: Attempts to remove learned influence or concepts require explicit success definitions and adversarial evaluation.

nodes.title: Classical predictive ML
nodes.summary: Classifiers, regressors, trees and ensembles form an essential baseline beyond LLMs.

nodes.title: Convolutional networks
nodes.summary: Image-oriented convolutional architectures with spatial feature extraction.

nodes.title: Decoder-only autoregressive language models
nodes.summary: Generate token sequences conditioned on preceding context; distinguish base and instruction-tuned checkpoints.

nodes.title: Diffusion generative models
nodes.summary: Generative processes learned through noise-related denoising objectives, not a single backbone architecture.

nodes.title: Diffusion transformers
nodes.summary: Transformer backbones used for diffusion; not equivalent to autoregressive language modeling.

nodes.title: Embedding and reranking models
nodes.summary: Representations and scoring models supporting retrieval and similarity workflows.

nodes.title: Encoder-decoder models
nodes.summary: Separate source encoding and conditional sequence decoding.

nodes.title: Encoder-only language models
nodes.summary: Bidirectional encoders used in representation learning and discriminative tasks.

nodes.title: Flow-matching generative models
nodes.summary: Related continuous generative modeling objectives requiring their own objective and sampler labels.

nodes.title: Generative adversarial networks
nodes.summary: Generator-discriminator training; the word adversarial here does not imply malicious use.

nodes.title: Latent diffusion pipelines
nodes.summary: Diffusion operates in a learned latent space, with separate encoding and decoding components.

nodes.title: Mixture-of-experts models
nodes.summary: Sparse expert routing is a component choice that can coexist with transformer backbones.

nodes.title: Neural networks
nodes.summary: Parameterized differentiable models; a shared prerequisite, not a specific generative family.

nodes.title: State-space and hybrid sequence models
nodes.summary: Alternative or hybrid sequence computation; transformer-specific edits do not transfer automatically.

nodes.title: Transformers
nodes.summary: Attention-based blocks used in multiple modeling objectives and modalities.

nodes.title: U-Net-style diffusion backbones
nodes.summary: Convolutional multiscale denoisers often used within image diffusion pipelines.

nodes.title: Variational autoencoders
nodes.summary: Latent-variable encoders and decoders; can also be components of larger generative pipelines.

nodes.title: Vision-language models
nodes.summary: Coupled visual representations and language processing introduce multiple input pathways.

nodes.title: Malicious adapters or adapter substitution
nodes.summary: Distribute or apply an attacker-controlled adaptation artifact to alter behavior.
nodes.caveat: Adapter format alone does not establish a backdoor; this is a composed threat scenario needing artifact-specific evidence.

nodes.title: Tool-loop and recursive-delegation exhaustion
nodes.summary: Induce repeated actions or delegated calls when agent execution lacks effective budgets.
nodes.caveat: Model reasoning, tool cost and wall-clock limits require separate accounting.

nodes.title: Artifact, adapter or configuration substitution
nodes.summary: Replace a trusted distribution object with an unreviewed version or misleading identity.
nodes.caveat: A hash provides integrity only relative to a trusted expected value and provenance.

nodes.title: Model inversion and attribute inference
nodes.summary: Infer sensitive attributes or input-related information from model behavior and auxiliary knowledge.
nodes.caveat: Attribute inference, prototype reconstruction and exact example extraction are different outcomes.

nodes.title: Trigger-conditioned model backdoors
nodes.summary: Implant attacker-selected behavior activated by a trigger while retaining ordinary utility.
nodes.caveat: Record trigger, target behavior, clean utility and attack success separately.

nodes.title: Prompt-cache timing inference
nodes.summary: Use observable service timing to investigate shared caching or prior prompt use.
nodes.caveat: Cache sharing and a statistically usable signal must be demonstrated, not assumed.

nodes.title: AI-assisted harmful activity
nodes.summary: Use generation, analysis or automation for harmful purposes without necessarily breaking the model.
nodes.caveat: Describe the risk category without shipping operational harmful payloads or unauthorized target automation.

nodes.title: Evidence and citation laundering
nodes.summary: Make untrustworthy content appear authoritative through generated references or retrieval chains.
nodes.caveat: Editorial scenario, not an automatically established empirical attack for every citation system.

nodes.title: Agent or connector confused-deputy abuse
nodes.summary: Induce a more-privileged component to exercise authority for an unauthorized requester.
nodes.caveat: Protocol authentication and semantic action authorization are separate checks.

nodes.title: Malicious dependencies or repository code
nodes.summary: Compromise the application through imported code, plugins or build dependencies.
nodes.caveat: Traditional software supply-chain controls remain necessary around AI artifacts.

nodes.title: Evasion of an ML security detector
nodes.summary: Modify an input to avoid a specific classifier or deployed detector.
nodes.caveat: Specify the detector and evasion metric; do not infer operational malware evasion from a generic image experiment.

nodes.title: Diffusion backdoors / BadDiffusion
nodes.summary: Alter training or diffusion processes to produce attacker-chosen outcomes under a trigger.
nodes.caveat: Sampler and process-specific assumptions must be retained; no automatic applicability to every flow or DiT model.

nodes.title: Diffusion training-image extraction
nodes.summary: Recover or closely reproduce training images under the conditions studied in extraction research.
nodes.caveat: Specify similarity thresholds, reference corpus and deduplication; do not substitute intuition for evidence.

nodes.title: Direct prompt injection
nodes.summary: Attacker-supplied instructions attempt to override application task or trust policy.
nodes.caveat: Direct access does not imply control over privileged system messages.

nodes.title: Unauthorized teacher-student capability transfer
nodes.summary: Apply distillation or imitation to acquire capabilities without required permission.
nodes.caveat: Distillation is neutral; the adversarial label depends on authorization and use, not the algorithm name.

nodes.title: Benchmark or evaluation contamination
nodes.summary: Influence measurement by leaking evaluation material into training or changing the evaluation set.
nodes.caveat: Benign overlap, deliberate contamination and judge manipulation are separate phenomena.

nodes.title: Exploitation of excessive delegated agency
nodes.summary: Turn broadly granted tools or missing approvals into unauthorized actions.
nodes.caveat: Excessive agency is an enabling weakness; the attacking mechanism must still be identified.

nodes.title: Unauthorized factual model editing
nodes.summary: Modify selected model associations to influence later answers.
nodes.caveat: ROME is neutral research; unauthorized application is the threat scenario and needs separate authorization context.

nodes.title: Gradient-based adversarial perturbations / FGSM
nodes.summary: Use input gradients to find perturbations that affect predictions.
nodes.caveat: Specify perturbation set, preprocessing and target task.

nodes.title: Gradient-guided adversarial suffixes
nodes.summary: Optimize discrete prompt suffixes through model or surrogate gradient information.
nodes.caveat: White-box construction must not be mislabeled as purely black-box discovery.

nodes.title: Reconstruction from gradients or updates
nodes.summary: Recover information about training inputs from exposed gradients or model updates.
nodes.caveat: Requires update visibility; ordinary text API access does not supply it.

nodes.title: Indirect prompt injection
nodes.summary: Lower-trust documents or tool content carry instructions that an application treats as authority.
nodes.caveat: The external content must be ingested and affect a privileged workflow.

nodes.title: Jailbreaking and refusal bypass
nodes.summary: Elicit behavior outside an operator's intended model behavior constraints.
nodes.caveat: Not every prompt injection is a jailbreak and not every jailbreak exposes confidential data.

nodes.title: Automated judge or grader manipulation
nodes.summary: Influence grading instructions, context or feedback so a system appears more successful or safe.
nodes.caveat: Coverage scenario; needs judge-specific validation before publishing an empirical success claim.

nodes.title: Many-shot context attacks
nodes.summary: Use long sequences of demonstrations to steer behavior in the studied long-context setting.
nodes.caveat: Context capacity, sampling and target version materially affect results.

nodes.title: Membership inference
nodes.summary: Estimate whether a candidate record was included in a model's training set.
nodes.caveat: Requires a meaningful candidate and baseline; membership inference is not full-record reconstruction.

nodes.title: Persistent agent-memory poisoning
nodes.summary: Plant or induce stored entries that redirect future tasks or decisions.
nodes.caveat: Persistence must be tested across sessions; an instruction in one prompt is not sufficient evidence.

nodes.title: Behavioral tampering through merges or conversion
nodes.summary: Introduce an untrusted component or update while transforming a model artifact.
nodes.caveat: A composite scenario, not evidence that ordinary merging or quantization is intrinsically malicious.

nodes.title: Black-box functional model extraction
nodes.summary: Train a substitute to imitate target behavior from queried outputs.
nodes.caveat: Functional fidelity is not equality of weights; query rights and licensing are separate policy questions.

nodes.title: Inter-agent trust and message manipulation
nodes.summary: Influence delegated workflows through messages treated as instructions or trusted results.
nodes.caveat: Composed threat scenario; a multi-agent framework paper is architecture background, not attack proof.

nodes.title: Instructions carried through multimodal content
nodes.summary: Lower-trust visible text or interpreted media can become instructions in a multimodal workflow.
nodes.caveat: This is a scope-level extension; a visual adversarial perturbation is a separate mechanism.

nodes.title: Improper handling of model-generated output
nodes.summary: A downstream application treats model output as executable or privileged input without appropriate validation.
nodes.caveat: The unsafe sink is an application vulnerability; a model need not be specially trained or jailbroken.

nodes.title: Iterative projected adversarial optimization
nodes.summary: Evaluate robustness with iterative constrained perturbation search.
nodes.caveat: A weak attack or gradient masking can falsely suggest robustness.

nodes.title: Physical-world adversarial examples
nodes.summary: Study perturbations after printing, capture or other real-world transformations.
nodes.caveat: Digital success does not imply physical success; transformations are part of the threat model.

nodes.title: Preference or reward-signal manipulation
nodes.summary: Influence comparisons, reward models or feedback used in post-training.
nodes.caveat: Coverage node grounded in threat modeling; not a named-paper claim that all DPO systems are vulnerable.

nodes.title: Pretraining data poisoning
nodes.summary: Influence learned behavior by contributing or changing data before broad training.
nodes.caveat: Effective influence depends on ingestion, filtering, mixture weights and training dynamics.

nodes.title: Partial parameter recovery from API behavior
nodes.summary: Recover a model projection component or dimensions under specific query and score assumptions.
nodes.caveat: Partial projection recovery is not complete recovery of a production model.

nodes.title: System or developer prompt disclosure
nodes.summary: Attempt to disclose hidden configuration text supplied to the model.
nodes.caveat: Disclosure alone is not proof of a security compromise; secrets should not rely on prompt secrecy.

nodes.title: Unauthorized retrieved-document disclosure
nodes.summary: Reveal content the requesting principal should not be authorized to retrieve or view.
nodes.caveat: A missing access check is an application authorization failure, not necessarily training-data memorization.

nodes.title: RAG knowledge-base poisoning
nodes.summary: Insert or modify retrieved evidence to steer generated answers or decisions.
nodes.caveat: Knowledge corruption is not necessarily an instruction-bearing prompt injection.

nodes.title: Adversarial refusal-direction modification
nodes.summary: Apply a refusal-related intervention to bypass a studied model constraint.
nodes.caveat: Weight-edit variants may also need activation measurement and calibration; other safeguards may remain.

nodes.title: Retrieval and ranking manipulation
nodes.summary: Influence which attacker-controlled material is selected as evidence.
nodes.caveat: Search discoverability, ranking and actual answer influence must be measured independently.

nodes.title: Adversarial fine-tuning to alter constraints
nodes.summary: Use training control to modify a model's refusal or other behavioral properties.
nodes.caveat: Benign fine-tuning can also cause regressions; malicious intent and accidental regression are distinct labels.

nodes.title: Cross-session or cross-tenant disclosure
nodes.summary: Expose another principal's data through state, context assembly, caching or access-control failures.
nodes.caveat: Separate actual content leakage from a timing signal that only suggests prior use.

nodes.title: Instruction-tuning data poisoning
nodes.summary: Corrupt demonstrations or labels used during supervised adaptation.
nodes.caveat: A data-contribution threat differs from complete control of a fine-tuning job.

nodes.title: Persistent conditional LLM backdoors
nodes.summary: Study intentionally implanted conditional behavior that can survive tested safety-training procedures.
nodes.caveat: Not evidence of spontaneous deception or universal resistance to every defense.

nodes.title: Energy and latency amplification / sponge inputs
nodes.summary: Construct expensive inputs for particular model and execution configurations.
nodes.caveat: Hardware and implementation assumptions limit transfer.

nodes.title: Adversarial activation steering
nodes.summary: Use runtime intervention to influence behavior without changing stored weights.
nodes.caveat: Needs the identified intervention surface and evaluation; steering is not always malicious.

nodes.title: Token, context and inference-budget exhaustion
nodes.summary: Cause excessive permitted work through input/output length or uncontrolled request behavior.
nodes.caveat: Separate bounded expensive requests from sustained denial of service and per-tenant quota failure.

nodes.title: Tool-description poisoning
nodes.summary: Influence tool selection or actions through attacker-controlled tool metadata.
nodes.caveat: Client trust behavior and descriptor availability determine exposure.

nodes.title: Tool-output injection
nodes.summary: Return lower-trust instructions in a tool response to redirect an agent.
nodes.caveat: Tool execution success is not equivalent to authority for the response's instructions.

nodes.title: Tool definition or behavior changes after approval
nodes.summary: Change a tool after it has acquired user or client trust.
nodes.caveat: Record version and approval-binding assumptions; metadata changes alone do not prove exploitation.

nodes.title: Language-model training-data extraction
nodes.summary: Recover training-specific text through model interaction in a setting that permits verification.
nodes.caveat: Verbatim-looking output is not proof of membership without a verification method; some procedures use scoring signals.

nodes.title: Transfer of adversarial prompts
nodes.summary: Apply an attack constructed on a source model to a different target.
nodes.caveat: Receiving a precomputed suffix is different from having optimized it using only the target API.

nodes.title: Unsafe checkpoint deserialization
nodes.summary: A loader executes or interprets malicious artifact content during model loading.
nodes.caveat: Do not conflate parser/code-execution risk with a learned backdoor.

nodes.title: Optimized visual jailbreaks
nodes.summary: Use adversarial visual perturbations to affect a vision-language model's safety behavior.
nodes.caveat: Distinct from simply placing readable instructions inside an image.

nodes.title: Unauthorized checkpoint or adapter theft
nodes.summary: Acquire exact artifacts through storage, account or supply-chain compromise.
nodes.caveat: Ordinary download of intentionally public weights is not theft.

nodes.title: Architectural applicability versus empirical evidence
nodes.summary: A compatible surface is not an experimental demonstration of attack effectiveness.

nodes.title: Attention and cross-attention
nodes.summary: Attention mechanisms combine representations; cross-attention introduces distinct conditioning surfaces.

nodes.title: Trust boundaries and authorization
nodes.summary: Track where data, instructions and authority cross from one principal or component to another.

nodes.title: Text, image and control conditioning
nodes.summary: Conditioning can enter through text encoders, cross-attention or additional control branches.

nodes.title: Context windows and in-context learning
nodes.summary: Information in the current context is different from information encoded in persistent weights.

nodes.title: Sampling and decoding configuration
nodes.summary: Temperature, selection rules and stopping conditions affect generated outputs without retraining.

nodes.title: Input and output embeddings
nodes.summary: Token or modality representations differ from a vector database entry and from output projection weights.

nodes.title: Losses, gradients and optimization
nodes.summary: Training signals and their visibility matter for optimization attacks and privacy leakage.

nodes.title: Classifier-free guidance
nodes.summary: A generative guidance mechanism, not a safety-policy classifier.

nodes.title: KV caches and prefix reuse
nodes.summary: Inference-state caching can create isolation and timing considerations depending on implementation.

nodes.title: Latent spaces and codecs
nodes.summary: Latent representations, encoders and decoders contribute separate generative-system surfaces.

nodes.title: Logits, probabilities and observable outputs
nodes.summary: API output granularity changes what an attacker can infer or optimize.

nodes.title: Memorization, generalization and duplication
nodes.summary: Retaining training-specific information is distinct from merely learning a distribution.

nodes.title: Noise schedules and denoising objectives
nodes.summary: Noise parameterization and time steps distinguish diffusion-specific interventions.

nodes.title: Weights, parameters and activations
nodes.summary: Distinguish persistent learned tensors from input-dependent intermediate activations.

nodes.title: Residual streams and block structure
nodes.summary: Shared representation pathways are relevant to localized activation and weight interventions.

nodes.title: Diffusion and flow samplers
nodes.summary: Inference schedules and solvers affect cost and outcomes independently of weights.

nodes.title: Tokenization and vocabulary
nodes.summary: Text segmentation and special tokens are part of the model input contract.

nodes.title: Attack transferability
nodes.summary: Success on one model or configuration does not establish success on a different target.

nodes.title: Risk-based human approval
nodes.summary: Require informed approval for high-impact actions without presenting approval as a universal protection.

nodes.title: Enforce authorization outside the model
nodes.summary: Check the requesting principal, resource and action in deterministic application code.

nodes.title: Backdoor-oriented artifact evaluation
nodes.summary: Test conditional behavior and clean utility; absence of a found trigger is not a proof of absence.

nodes.title: Separate data from authority
nodes.summary: Keep lower-trust content from granting itself privileges; defense in depth, not a perfect prompt-only filter.

nodes.title: Request, token, tool and cost budgets
nodes.summary: Enforce per-principal limits and wall-clock or recursion boundaries outside model discretion.

nodes.title: Cache and session isolation
nodes.summary: Partition reusable state and measure information-sharing signals under realistic conditions.

nodes.title: Least-privilege contribution and CI pipeline
nodes.summary: Separate untrusted content inspection from credentials, deployment and executable builds.

nodes.title: Training-data minimization and deduplication
nodes.summary: Reduce unnecessary sensitive or repeated records; does not provide a formal privacy guarantee.

nodes.title: Responsible disclosure and safe research
nodes.summary: Use authorized test environments, minimize sensitive data, and preserve correction and retraction workflows.

nodes.title: Differentially private training
nodes.summary: Bound training contribution under a stated privacy definition and accounting procedure.

nodes.title: Sandboxing, egress and execution isolation
nodes.summary: Limit what compromised model-adjacent code or agents can execute and reach.

nodes.title: Least-privilege tools and scoped credentials
nodes.summary: Limit reachable actions and data; approval must bind to actual arguments and destinations.

nodes.title: Auditable action and content lineage
nodes.summary: Capture privacy-conscious provenance and tool decisions for investigation, not hidden reasoning extraction.

nodes.title: Memory provenance, review and expiry
nodes.summary: Record who introduced persistent state and allow scoped review, revocation and reset.

nodes.title: Context-specific output validation
nodes.summary: Treat generated code, markup and queries as untrusted input at their final sink.

nodes.title: Dataset and artifact provenance
nodes.summary: Record identities, immutable revisions, transformations and approval history.

nodes.title: Authorization-aware retrieval
nodes.summary: Filter by principal before disclosure and preserve access metadata through retrieval and generation.

nodes.title: Safety and utility regression testing
nodes.summary: Reevaluate changed checkpoints, adapters, merges and configurations on held-out tests.

nodes.title: Adversarial training and robustness evaluation
nodes.summary: Evaluate against an explicit perturbation set and adaptive attacks.

nodes.title: Safer tensor loading and dependency control
nodes.summary: Prefer constrained serialization and audited loaders while retaining parser and behavioral checks.

nodes.title: Adaptive defense evaluation
nodes.summary: Evaluate against an attacker who knows the defense rather than only stale fixed prompts.

nodes.title: AgentDojo benchmark
nodes.summary: A source-specific agent task and prompt-injection evaluation reference.

nodes.title: Attack success and severity
nodes.summary: Define a measurable success event; distinguish model text from a consequential tool action.

nodes.title: Query, token, latency and compute cost
nodes.summary: Report budgets and resource impact with the exact experimental configuration.

nodes.title: Claim strength and verification depth
nodes.summary: Separate theory, empirical reporting, independent reproduction, deployment reports and editorial hypotheses.

nodes.title: Extraction fidelity versus artifact equality
nodes.summary: Compare functional agreement, task quality and parameter recovery without conflating them.

nodes.title: HarmBench benchmark
nodes.summary: A source-specific red-team and robust refusal evaluation reference.

nodes.title: Privacy verification and baselines
nodes.summary: Use membership baselines, record verification, confidence and task-appropriate similarity criteria.

nodes.title: Reproducibility and statistical uncertainty
nodes.summary: Store seeds, versions, sampling rules, test split and confidence intervals where meaningful.

nodes.title: Explicit threat model
nodes.summary: State goals, capabilities, prior knowledge, budgets, authority and target revisions.

nodes.title: Transfer and architecture boundaries
nodes.summary: Distinguish source-model success, target-model transfer, adaptation and unsupported generalization.

nodes.title: Clean utility and false positives
nodes.summary: Measure normal task completion and overblocking alongside attacks.

nodes.title: Agent authority and workflow attacks
nodes.summary: Redirect tool use, memory or inter-agent workflows across trust boundaries.

nodes.title: Availability and cost attacks
nodes.summary: Exploit resource allocation, input cost or uncontrolled loops.

nodes.title: Evaluation and accountability attacks
nodes.summary: Distort measurement or evade a specific oversight control.

nodes.title: Adversarial input evasion
nodes.summary: Perturb inputs or their presentation to change predictions or guardrail decisions.

nodes.title: Capability misuse
nodes.summary: Use a legitimate model capability for harmful activity without assuming model compromise.

nodes.title: Poisoning, backdoors and persistence
nodes.summary: Corrupt inputs to learning or persistent state to influence later behavior.

nodes.title: Privacy inference and data extraction
nodes.summary: Infer or reconstruct protected data under different visibility assumptions.

nodes.title: Prompt and context manipulation
nodes.summary: Attacks that reinterpret or override instructions through model-visible inputs.

nodes.title: Representation and weight interventions
nodes.summary: White-box model modifications and runtime interventions applied adversarially.

nodes.title: Retrieval and knowledge manipulation
nodes.summary: Influence external evidence, selection, authorization or attribution.

nodes.title: Supply-chain and runtime compromise
nodes.summary: Compromise loaders, artifacts, dependencies or hosting components.

nodes.title: Model artifact theft and functional extraction
nodes.summary: Acquire artifacts or reproduce behavior with distinct threat models.

nodes.title: Training and adaptation abuse
nodes.summary: Attacker-influenced data, objectives or updates can change model behavior.

nodes.title: Compiled inference engines
nodes.summary: Executable optimized plans, distinct from data-only weight containers.

nodes.title: GGUF
nodes.summary: Binary tensor/metadata packaging; can store different numerical types and supported architectures.

nodes.title: Complete model package
nodes.summary: Weights alone are insufficient: tokenizer, config, templates, revisions and auxiliary modules affect behavior.

nodes.title: ONNX
nodes.summary: Interchange representation with computational graphs, operators and parameters.

nodes.title: PyTorch checkpoints and pickle-related loading
nodes.summary: Checkpoint extensions do not fully describe loading behavior or executable deserialization risk.

nodes.title: Safetensors
nodes.summary: Tensor serialization with a safer loading design; does not establish benign learned behavior.

nodes.title: Cause unauthorized actions or privilege use
nodes.summary: Redirect an agent or application into unauthorized tool calls, data access or changes.

nodes.title: Degrade availability or increase cost
nodes.summary: Exhaust capacity, latency, energy, tokens or tool budgets; distinguish algorithmic effects from generic request floods.

nodes.title: Violate intended behavioral constraints
nodes.summary: Cause the system to produce behavior its operator intends to disallow; includes safeguard bypass but not all output errors.

nodes.title: Manipulate outputs, predictions or decisions
nodes.summary: Change a task result, ranking, generated artifact or downstream decision in the attacker's favor.

nodes.title: Compromise the surrounding execution environment
nodes.summary: Exploit loaders, packages, plugins, build systems or integrations to compromise the host or distribution channel.

nodes.title: Evade security controls or accountability
nodes.summary: Defeat a deployed detector, monitoring or attribution control; metric-specific, not identical to refusal bypass.

nodes.title: Obtain protected information
nodes.summary: Infer or disclose training examples, attributes, prompts, retrieved records, session data or secrets without authorization.

nodes.title: Use AI to amplify harmful activity
nodes.summary: Adjacent misuse lens: abuse a capability without necessarily compromising the model or its host.

nodes.title: Appropriate model artifacts or capabilities
nodes.summary: Acquire weights, adapters or functional imitation; separate exact artifact theft from behavioral replication.

nodes.title: Establish persistent attacker influence
nodes.summary: Make attacker-selected behavior survive future sessions, triggers, updates or ordinary retraining.

nodes.title: Continued pretraining
nodes.summary: Further training on a continued or domain-specific objective; not necessarily instruction tuning.

nodes.title: Data collection, filtering and deduplication
nodes.summary: Dataset lineage and preprocessing affect privacy, integrity and evaluation reliability.

nodes.title: Deployment, monitoring and updates
nodes.summary: Packaging, serving and integration change security exposure beyond the model checkpoint.

nodes.title: Direct Preference Optimization
nodes.summary: A preference-learning objective; distinguish standard DPO from reward-model-plus-PPO training.

nodes.title: Evaluation data and benchmark governance
nodes.summary: Separate training, attack development, validation and final testing.

nodes.title: Post-training
nodes.summary: Umbrella for adaptation after pretraining, including but not limited to alignment.

nodes.title: Preference data and reward models
nodes.summary: Human or synthetic comparisons can influence post-training objectives.

nodes.title: Pretraining
nodes.summary: Initial broad learning from a training objective and corpus.

nodes.title: RLHF and policy optimization
nodes.summary: Learning from feedback may involve a reward model and policy optimization; not the only alignment route.

nodes.title: Safety and instruction tuning
nodes.summary: Intended behavioral constraints are learned properties that need evaluation after modifications.

nodes.title: Supervised fine-tuning
nodes.summary: Optimize on labeled demonstrations or input-output examples.

nodes.title: Tool-using agents
nodes.summary: A loop combines model decisions, tools, observations and policy enforcement.

nodes.title: Browser and computer-use integrations
nodes.summary: Rendered pages and document content can become model observations and trigger actions.

nodes.title: Evaluation pipelines and automated judges
nodes.summary: Judges, test sets and grading code are security-relevant dependencies.

nodes.title: Corpora, vector indexes and rerankers
nodes.summary: Chunking, embeddings and ranking influence which external content reaches a model.

nodes.title: Model loaders and executable repository code
nodes.summary: Parsing or importing model artifacts is a separate host-execution trust decision.

nodes.title: Persistent agent memory
nodes.summary: Stored summaries, preferences or instructions can influence later sessions.

nodes.title: Multi-agent orchestration
nodes.summary: Messages and delegated authority cross multiple component boundaries.

nodes.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
nodes.summary: Retrieval, ranking, authorization, prompt assembly and generation are separate components.

nodes.title: Model registries and distribution
nodes.summary: Artifacts, revisions, licenses and upstream dependencies need provenance.

nodes.title: Inference engines and serving gateways
nodes.summary: Batching, caches, request isolation and scheduling are runtime properties.

nodes.title: Tools, plugins, MCP and connectors
nodes.summary: Descriptions, arguments, outputs, identity and authorization are distinct tool surfaces.

nodes.title: Hugging Face Diffusers
nodes.summary: Composable generative pipelines and scheduler tooling.

nodes.title: llama.cpp
nodes.summary: Inference runtime commonly associated with GGUF artifacts.

nodes.title: MLX
nodes.summary: Array and ML framework often used in Apple-silicon environments.

nodes.title: TensorRT / TensorRT-adjacent serving
nodes.summary: Optimization and execution ecosystem requiring explicit engine and plugin trust.

nodes.title: Hugging Face Transformers
nodes.summary: Model training/inference library; separate from transformer architecture.

nodes.title: Unsloth
nodes.summary: Efficiency-oriented model tooling; not pretraining, post-training, architecture or file format.

nodes.title: vLLM
nodes.summary: Serving runtime with version-dependent scheduling and caching behavior.

nodes.title: Checkpoint conversion and sharding
nodes.summary: Repackage representations and metadata; compatibility and integrity are separate questions.

nodes.title: GPTQ
nodes.summary: A specific post-training weight-quantization method, not a general model family.

nodes.title: Model and adapter merging
nodes.summary: Combine compatible parameters or updates; provenance and behavioral regressions must be reassessed.

nodes.title: Pruning and sparsity
nodes.summary: Remove or constrain parameters/connections; security effects are not guaranteed by compression.

nodes.title: Quantization and numerical precision
nodes.summary: Change numerical representation, often with calibration; separate from serialization and training stage.

access_profiles.title: Output-query access
access_profiles.caveat: No weights, logits, training data or privileged context are implied.

access_profiles.title: Score or logit API access
access_profiles.caveat: Specify score precision, top-k restrictions and any allowed logit transformations.

access_profiles.title: White-box or surrogate optimization
access_profiles.caveat: A surrogate and target must be separately identified; transfer is not guaranteed.

access_profiles.title: External-context authoring
access_profiles.caveat: Victim must actually ingest the lower-trust content; attacker does not control system instructions.

access_profiles.title: Retrieval-corpus contribution
access_profiles.caveat: Insertion, ranking and ingestion permissions vary; corpus write does not imply tool authority.

access_profiles.title: Tool metadata or response influence
access_profiles.caveat: Registration, version changes and output control are distinct subvariants.

access_profiles.title: Activation intervention
access_profiles.caveat: Requires compatible runtime hooks; ordinary API prompting is insufficient.

access_profiles.title: Readable model artifacts
access_profiles.caveat: Weights, adapters or configurations are readable; distinguish public access from unauthorized access.

access_profiles.title: Writable or replaceable model artifacts
access_profiles.caveat: Use separate calibration/runtime-read capabilities where the method requires them.

access_profiles.title: Training-data contribution
access_profiles.caveat: Data must enter an actual training run; ingestion and effective influence are additional conditions.

access_profiles.title: Training or fine-tuning control
access_profiles.caveat: Specify trainable tensors, data, objective, compute and restrictions of a hosted service.

access_profiles.title: Agent-exposed capability
access_profiles.caveat: Success additionally depends on delegated tools, policy enforcement and reachable resources.

access_profiles.title: Dependency or package distribution
access_profiles.caveat: Victim must install, import or execute the affected artifact.

access_profiles.title: Observable shared-service timing
access_profiles.caveat: Shared state, noise, isolation and repeatable signal must be established.

access_profiles.title: Candidate records and auxiliary knowledge
access_profiles.caveat: Membership/attribute methods need baselines; extra scores or shadow data are variant-specific.

access_profiles.title: Shared gradients or updates
access_profiles.caveat: Not an ordinary text-only API setting; batching and defenses change feasibility.

access_profiles.title: Persistent-memory influence
access_profiles.caveat: Attacker-controlled content must persist and be used in later decisions.

access_profiles.title: Image/audio/video input influence
access_profiles.caveat: Perturbation limits and modality preprocessing are part of the threat model.

access_profiles.title: Inference configuration control
access_profiles.caveat: Sampling settings, system prompts and model weights are distinct privileges.

access_profiles.title: Evaluation or feedback influence
access_profiles.caveat: Judge prompts, benchmark data, labels and reward signals are separate subvariants.

access_profiles.title: Model-output reaches an unsafe sink
access_profiles.caveat: An application must consume output as code, markup, queries or another privileged form.

relation_types.rule: Only the prerequisite subgraph must be acyclic.

relation_types.meaning: Technique belongs to an editorial family
relation_types.rule: Canonical node may be cross-listed without duplication.

relation_types.meaning: Technique can contribute to this goal
relation_types.rule: Not an unconditional success or authorization claim.

relation_types.meaning: Topic is relevant to architecture or component
relation_types.rule: Scope only; empirical demonstrations require observation records.

relation_types.meaning: Source uses a neutral method or component
relation_types.rule: Does not automatically label the target method malicious.

relation_types.meaning: Source is a narrower instance of target
relation_types.rule: Do not use for merely similar outcomes.

relation_types.meaning: Source may enable a later technique
relation_types.rule: Chain conditions must be explicit; never assume transitive exploitability.
Symmetric; serialize one sorted endpoint pair.

relation_types.meaning: Control addresses part of a threat
relation_types.rule: Must state conditions and residual risk.

relation_types.meaning: Topic links to a suitable evaluation concept
relation_types.rule: Benchmark suitability is scope-limited, not proof that it already covers the technique.
Derived from references; not proof that every sentence is supported.
Derived from Markdown links; never infer an attack prerequisite.

relation_types.meaning: A specific claim is supported by a source
relation_types.rule: Use claim records with locator, limits and verification depth.

relation_types.meaning: A specific claim has contrary evidence
relation_types.rule: Do not silently replace or erase contrary findings.

relation_types.meaning: Record has a newer canonical successor
relation_types.rule: Keep redirects and history; do not delete externally referenced IDs.

observations.limitations: Architecture and model identity only; exact checkpoint hashes and experiment-level access must be added from full text.

observations.limitations: No claim of universal or complete safety removal; model list and revisions must be verified before model-specific badges.

observations.limitations: No universal success rate or applicability claim for all diffusion and flow models.

observations.limitations: Historical study, not a statement about current API vulnerability or complete model-weight recovery.

research_backlog.topic: MoE routing, speculative decoding and test-time-compute attacks

research_backlog.requirement: Distinguish failure of a stated deletion criterion from general model jailbreaks.

research_backlog.topic: Model-edit variants, causal tracing and mechanistic interpretability
research_backlog.requirement: Add method prerequisites and measurement limits rather than assuming causal proof from steering success.
Verify advisory, affected/fixed versions and prerequisites; never infer a product CVE from a paper title.

research_backlog.requirement: Add official documentation and versioned integration surfaces, without classifying wrappers as architectures.
Add verified Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Stable Diffusion and flow-model package profiles with exact revisions; no inherited vulnerability claims.

research_backlog.topic: RLVR, reasoning optimization, RLAIF and policy-optimization variants
research_backlog.requirement: Explain training objective, source of feedback and inference compute separately; verify primary sources.
Add recurrent, graph-neural, audio, video, robotics and vision-language-action profiles when supported by sourced security routes.

research_backlog.topic: OWASP LLM 2026 and agentic category crosswalks
research_backlog.requirement: Read the exact edition, then map each external ID explicitly; retain verified 2025 mapping as historical.
Prioritize USENIX, IEEE S&P, ACM CCS, NDSS, DEF CON, Black Hat and CCC official pages; verify video identity and timestamps separately.
